home.title: Vessel
home.lead: A VPN service run by the anoni.net anonymous network community. Its connections are disguised, so their packets are hard to recognize as VPN traffic and get through more easily on networks that block VPNs. You sign up without an email address or phone number, and the keys for your connection are made in your own browser, so the service's servers never have them.
home.inviteOnly: Invites come from community members only, and places are limited.
how.title: How it works
how.1.title: Redeem an invite
how.1.body: Enter your invite code and you get a 16-digit account number. You sign in with it from then on.
how.2.title: Add a device
how.2.body: Pick the city of the node, name the device, and choose whether to block malicious sites and ads. Keys are generated in your browser, and the private key never reaches the service's servers.
how.3.title: Import into the app
how.3.body: Scan the QR code with the AmneziaWG app or import the downloaded file, then switch it on.
limits.title: What Vessel protects
limits.lead: Vessel protects the connection between your device and the node: your network provider cannot see where you go, and has a harder time telling that you use a VPN. Past the node, sites see the node's IP address, but they still see the accounts you sign in to and what you do.
limits.can.1: Your network provider sees only that you connect to a Vessel node, not where you go from there
limits.can.2: The connection is disguised, so it is less likely to be recognized and blocked as a VPN
limits.can.3: You can reach sites that are blocked on your network
limits.can.4: You can choose to block malicious sites or ads, filtered by the node's DNS resolver, which keeps no query logs
limits.cannot.1: It does not make you anonymous: the service's nodes can see which domains you connect to. Use Tor Browser when you need anonymity
limits.cannot.2: It does not hide your accounts: once you sign in to Google or Facebook, they still know it is you
limits.cannot.3: It cannot guarantee that every network lets it through, since blocking keeps changing
data.title: What we keep
data.kept.1: A hash of your account number, which cannot be turned back into the number
data.kept.2: When the account was created and last signed in to
data.kept.3: Each device's name, public key, city and expiry date
data.notKept.1: Email, phone number or any other contact details
data.notKept.3: Where you connect to, or when
data.cloudflare: This site goes through Cloudflare, which can see visitors' IP addresses and the pages they view.
data.stats: Views of public pages, and the result of each step of redeeming, signing in and creating a device, go to the Umami instance anoni.net hosts so problems along the way show up. Umami works out the country and city from the IP address but does not keep the address. Account numbers, device names and settings, and keys are never sent.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.invite.q: How do I get an invite code?
faq.invite.a: During the test, codes go out through the anoni.net newsletter, one per subscriber. Places are limited, and whether more go out depends on how the first round is used.
faq.cost.a: No. Volunteers run it. Plans for after the test will be announced separately.
faq.lost.q: What if I lose my account number?
faq.lost.a: It cannot be recovered. The service has no email address for you and keeps only a hash of the number, so you would need a new invite code. A password manager is a good place to keep it.
faq.number.q: The account number is only digits. Is that safe?
faq.number.a: Sixteen digits give ten quadrillion combinations, and sign-in attempts are rate limited, so guessing is not practical. The database stores only a keyed hash of the number, which is hard to reverse even if the database leaks.
faq.share.q: Can my family use my account?
faq.share.a: An account holds up to 3 devices sharing 50 GB a month, so family devices are fine. Anyone with the account number can also see and delete your devices, so share it only with people you trust. Accounts and invite codes must not be sold.
faq.protocols.q: How do VPN, WireGuard and AmneziaWG relate?
faq.protocols.a: VPN is the general name for services that send your connection through another server before it goes out. VPNs connect in different ways, called protocols, and WireGuard is one of them: simple, fast and used by many VPN apps. AmneziaWG is an open-source project built from WireGuard that adds a disguise, so connections are harder to recognize as a VPN and get through more easily on networks that block VPNs. Vessel uses AmneziaWG.
faq.maker.a: The Amnezia team, and its code is public on GitHub for anyone to check. Vessel has no direct affiliation with Amnezia. Get the app from its official store page or GitHub; the links in the setup steps all point to official sources.
faq.app.q: Why can't I use the regular WireGuard® app?
faq.app.a: Vessel disguises its connections with AmneziaWG, so its packets look different from regular WireGuard, and the regular app cannot use the config.
faq.ios.q: AmneziaWG is missing from my App Store
faq.ios.a: It is not listed in some regions. iPhones have no other way to install it, so the only option is an Apple ID from another region. On Android you can install the APK instead.
faq.twoDevices.q: Can I use one config on two devices?
faq.twoDevices.a: No. Two devices connected at once keep taking the connection from each other and drop out often. Create a config for each device, up to 3 per account.
faq.newPhone.q: What about a new phone or a reinstall?
faq.newPhone.a: A config is shown only once, when it is created, and the service's servers do not have the private key. Delete the old device from your list and create a new one.
faq.filter.q: Which domain filter should I pick?
faq.filter.a: Blocking malicious sites uses HaGeZi's Threat Intelligence Feeds (mini), and blocking ads adds HaGeZi Multi (Normal). The lists are updated every 8 hours. If unsure, pick no filtering. The ad list sometimes blocks sites that work fine. To change it later, delete the device and create it again. Browsers with “secure DNS” turned on skip the filter.
faq.trouble.a: Make sure AmneziaWG is up to date, then try another network, such as mobile data instead of Wi-Fi. If it still fails, delete the device and create it again. The disguise makes blocking less likely, but no network is guaranteed to work.
faq.speed.a: It depends on your network and how far you are from the node. In tests from Taiwan to the Singapore node, latency was about 67 ms and speed about 200 Mbps.
faq.cities.q: Will there be nodes in other cities?
faq.cities.a: Singapore is the only one for now. More will follow depending on how the test goes.
faq.expire.a: If an account does not sign in to the portal for 30 days, its devices expire and go offline, so unused configs do not linger on the nodes. Each sign-in extends them by 30 days.
faq.quota.a: The account's devices pause and resume automatically at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the month. Nothing needs to be set up again.
faq.p2p.a: The terms ban BitTorrent and other P2P file sharing during the test. Nodes also block outgoing TCP port 25, so you cannot send mail straight to a mail server on port 25. Port 587, which mail apps normally use, is not affected.
faq.see.q: Can the service see what I do?
faq.see.a: Nodes handle the domains and IP addresses you connect to, but not the contents of HTTPS connections. Nodes keep no logs of them, and the DNS resolvers do not log queries. Using a VPN moves the trust you place in your network provider to the service. Use Tor Browser when you need anonymity.
faq.law.q: What would the service hand over to law enforcement?
faq.law.a: Only what is listed under “What we keep”. There are no connection logs, so an exit IP address and a time cannot be traced to an account.
faq.cloudflare.q: Why does the portal go through Cloudflare?
faq.cloudflare.a: To stop attack traffic. Cloudflare can see visitors' IP addresses and the pages they view. VPN connections do not go through Cloudflare.
faq.delete.q: How do I delete my account?
faq.delete.a: Delete it on the account page. All devices disconnect right away and the data is deleted with them. Database backups disappear after their retention period, which the privacy policy states.

dns.title: DNS filtering
dns.lead: When you create a device you can have Vessel's DNS block malicious sites and ads. By default nothing is filtered.
dns.check.title: Check the current filter
dns.check.body: Press the button on a device connected to Vessel. The page connects to four test addresses on anoni.net; Vessel's resolvers hide some of them, and which ones go through shows the filter in effect.
dns.check.offline: The test addresses cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.
dns.check.notVessel: This browser is not using Vessel's DNS. The VPN may be off, or the browser may have “secure DNS” turned on. If you just switched connections, wait a minute and try again.
dns.check.none: Using Vessel's DNS, with no filtering.
dns.check.malware: Using Vessel's DNS, blocking malicious sites.
dns.check.ads: Using Vessel's DNS, blocking malicious sites and ads.
dns.check.mixed: The results do not agree. Wait a minute and check again.
dns.check.privacy: The test addresses go through Cloudflare to anoni.net's servers, which keep no record of these connections.
dns.options.title: The three options
dns.option.none: Domains are looked up and nothing is blocked.
dns.option.malware: Uses HaGeZi's Threat Intelligence Feeds (mini) to block about 425,000 domains that spread malware, phishing, scams and cryptomining, with few false positives.
dns.option.ads: Adds HaGeZi Multi (Normal), about 341,000 domains for ads, tracking, analytics and telemetry. It sometimes breaks part of an ordinary site.
dns.how.title: How it works
dns.how.body: Before a device connects to a site, it asks the resolver on the Vessel node for the domain. Domains on the list get a “no such domain” answer, so the connection never starts. The lists are updated every 8 hours and published on
dns.how.private: The resolvers keep no record of queries or of what they block, so Vessel has no “blocked so many times” figures. They validate DNSSEC and reject answers with bad signatures.
dns.limits.title: What it cannot do
dns.limits.1: Ads served from the same domain as the content, such as ads in YouTube videos
dns.limits.2: Main domains of common services such as Facebook and YouTube, which the list leaves alone so sites keep working
dns.limits.3: Queries from browsers with “secure DNS” turned on, or from apps that pick their own DNS, do not reach Vessel's resolvers
dns.limits.4: It sees only domains, not the path of a URL or the contents of HTTPS connections
dns.limits.5: It does not replace antivirus software, and it can block an ordinary site
dns.change.title: Changing it and reporting mistakes
dns.change.body: The filter is chosen when a device is created. To change it, delete the device and create it again. If an ordinary site is blocked, report it on the list's GitHub; the fix applies once the list is updated.
